public.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
public.description: Return the value of the deepest node that is an ancestor of both first and second, counting a node as its own ancestor. All tree values are unique; both target values exist and may be equal. The tree is nonempty. Trees use compact breadth-first arrays: read the root, then left and right child slots for each non-null node in queue order. null marks a missing child; absent trailing slots are null. [] is empty. Values are integers from -10000 to 10000 and there are at most 200 nodes.
hints: A target node can itself be the answer.
A node with targets in both child subtrees is their meeting point.
public.attribution: Original statement, examples, tests and solutions authored for Bekor, 2026, for a standard algorithmic problem. No third-party exercise text or solution code used.

javascript.signature: lowestCommonAncestor(values: (number | null)[], first: number, second: number): number

typescript.signature: lowestCommonAncestor(values: (number | null)[], first: number, second: number): number

explanation: Postorder search returns the encountered target or a subtree ancestor; a split across both children selects the current node. O(n) time and O(h) recursion space.
